summary: A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it preserves Add, adds the exact Upload API, uses the required multipart helper, validates inputs, and keeps the change scoped. B changes Add’s behavior and removes its existing test, both explicitly prohibited.
reasons: A leaves FilesService.Add unchanged, while B makes every Add body eagerly buffered with io.ReadAll, changing streaming, memory, and reader-error semantics contrary to the requirement to preserve Add’s behavior.
A performs explicit empty-filename and nil-content validation before encoding. B delegates both cases to multipartbody.NewFile without visible explicit validation.
A uses multipartbody.NewFile with field "file" and the supplied filename, producing a replayable body as required.

B weakens existing verification by replacing TestFilesService_Add instead of retaining it, contrary to the contract’s instruction not to weaken existing tests or repurpose Add into the retry fix path for this feature.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add’s option, request, decoding, and missing-data logic instead of routing through the existing Add method, directly violating the contract and creating maintenance drift; it should simply call s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...).
The retry test confirms two requests occur but does not inspect multipart filename, field, and content on both attempts, so it weakly verifies actual body replay.
No visible tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors, despite explicit test requirements.
risks_b: Changing Add to buffer arbitrary caller-provided bodies is an out-of-scope behavioral change and may impose unexpectedly large memory use.
Upload does not route through the public Add method; both methods instead bypass it through a new private add helper.
No visible validation or source-reader-error tests are added, and explicit prevalidation in Upload is absent from the visible implementation.
